title: Boss: the ReDoS post-incident actions
summary: The incident is over; the action items are yours. Rewrite two vulnerable rules, put a safety net around a legacy one, and make the customer search endpoint impossible to hang.

steps.title: INC-4471: action items
body: Last week a single request body pinned the API's CPU at 100% for 40 minutes. The post-incident review found four
places where untrusted text meets a regex, and assigned you the actions:
1. Rewrite the gateway's query-string rule, which a scan flagged as exponential.
2. Rewrite the hostname validator in the tenant settings page.
3. Put a timeout and a safe answer around a legacy rule that cannot change this sprint.
4. Make the customer log search safe for any pattern a customer types.
Every fix must still accept the valid inputs it accepted before.

steps.title: Rewrite the query-string rule
prompt: The gateway checks query strings with `^([^&=]+=[^&]*&?)+$`. On `a=a=a=...a=&&` it never returns.
The spec: one or more `name=value` pairs joined by single `&`. A name is one or more characters other than `=` and
`&`; a value is zero or more characters other than `=` and `&` (a literal `=` in a value arrives encoded as `%3D`).
Write a pattern for a whole query string that answers fast.

steps.title: Rewrite the hostname validator
prompt: Tenant settings validate custom hostnames with `^([a-z0-9]+-?)+(\.([a-z0-9]+-?)+)*$`, which hangs on 5,000 letters
followed by `!`.
The spec: one or more labels separated by single dots. A label is lower-case ASCII letters and digits, and may
contain hyphens, but not at its start or end. Several hyphens in a row are allowed: international names look like
`xn--bcher-kva`. Write a pattern for a whole hostname that answers fast.

steps.title: A safety net for the legacy rule
prompt: The comment validator uses `^(\w+\s?)*$`. Another team's import relies on its exact behaviour, so the pattern stays
**unchanged** this sprint (the rewrite is ticketed). Your job is the safety net.
Write `string Check(string input)`:
- Build the legacy regex **once** (a top-level variable above the method is fine) with a **50 ms** match timeout.
- Return `valid` or `invalid`.
- When matching times out, return `timeout after 50 ms`, built from the exception's `MatchTimeout` so it stays right
if someone changes the timeout.
Do not run it without the timeout: the last test is an attack input, and without a timeout it runs until the
checks are stopped.
solution: var legacy = new Regex(@"^(\w+\s?)*$", RegexOptions.None, TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(50));
template: Dojo.Eq("two words are valid", "valid", Check("hello world"));
Dojo.Eq("one trailing space is valid", "valid", Check("hello world "));
Dojo.Eq("a leading space is invalid", "invalid", Check(" hello"));
Dojo.Eq("the attack input times out safely", "timeout after 50 ms", Check(new string('a', 40) + "!"));

steps.title: Make the customer search impossible to hang
prompt: Customers search their logs with their own patterns. Write `string Search(string[] lines, string userPattern)`:
1. Build the regex with `RegexOptions.IgnoreCase | RegexOptions.NonBacktracking` and a 50 ms timeout.
2. If that throws `NotSupportedException` (the pattern needs lookarounds or backreferences), fall back to
`RegexOptions.IgnoreCase` alone, with the same 50 ms timeout.
3. If the pattern is invalid (`ArgumentException`), return `bad pattern`.
4. Count the lines with a match and return `N lines` (always `lines`, even for 0 or 1).
5. If matching times out, return `timeout`.
So most patterns run in linear time, and the few that need backtracking are still bounded.
`System.Text.RegularExpressions` is imported.
solution: regex = new Regex(userPattern, RegexOptions.IgnoreCase | RegexOptions.NonBacktracking, TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(50));
template: Dojo.Eq("a simple search, ignoring case", "2 lines", Search(dojoLines, "error|fatal"));
Dojo.Eq("(a+)+$ runs in linear time and finds nothing", "0 lines", Search(dojoLines, "(a+)+$"));
Dojo.Eq("a backreference falls back to backtracking", "4 lines", Search(dojoLines, @"(\w)\1"));
Dojo.Eq("a lookahead with a catastrophic body times out", "timeout", Search(new[] { new string('a', 40) + "!" }, @"^(?=\w)(\w+\s?)*$"));

require.message: Falls back when NonBacktracking is not supported
